appDetails.description:
This TA allows to add interaction features between TheHive or Cortex (https://www.strangebee.com/) and Splunk. It allows to retrieve all kind of information from TheHive/Cortex and to perform actions on these instances using Splunk, from a search or from a predefined dashboard.

This TA is supporting only TheHive 5. For having an app supporting TheHive 3 or 4, please check the oldest releases. It's also supporting the Cortex 3 version.

More information here: https://github.com/LetMeR00t/TA-thehive-cortex
appDetails.documentation:
The objective is to interface a SIEM tool such as Splunk in order to be able to perform automated tasks on observables/IOCs or TTPs.
This TA has been designed in such a way that :

- You can pull events periodically from TheHive about the different cases/alerts that were created or updated
- You can create new alert or case from Splunk in TheHive using the power of Splunk whether in a search or in a predefined dashboard.
- You can run a function in TheHive from an alert action
- You can interface Splunk Enterprise Security with TheHive
- You can retrieve information from Cortex about the different jobs that are being performed on the scanners.
- You can run new tasks from Splunk in Cortex using the power of Splunk whether in a search or a predefined dashboard.

If you need any documentation or help, please visit the related Github : https://github.com/LetMeR00t/TA-thehive-cortex

\# Release Notes - v4.2.2: "The Pollen Sieve" 🌼



\## Summary

Version 4.2.2 is a \*\*bug-fix release\*\* about things that used to fall through

without a sound. A custom field of type \`url\` was dropped from every alert and

case with no error at all; an empty "Job SID" let the create action fail deep

inside the add-on instead of stopping at the form. Both are fixed, and the

add-on now \*\*says something\*\* when it drops a custom field instead of staying

silent. Splunk Cloud administrators (\`sc\_admin\`) also regain write access to

the views and navigation.



No new feature is introduced and no configuration change is required — this is

a safe, drop-in update from v4.2.1.



\## Improvements & Bug Fixes



\### 🧩 Alert Actions: \`url\` custom fields are no longer dropped (\[#133]\(https://github.com/LetMeR00t/TA-thehive-cortex/issues/133))

\- \*\*Root cause\*\*: custom field values are only forwarded when their type is

  recognised by a chain handling \`string\`, \`boolean\`, \`integer\`, \`float\` and

  \`date\`. The \`url\` type, available since TheHive 5.1, was missing from that

  chain, so the field was skipped. The alert or case was still created, minus

  the field, and \*\*nothing was logged\*\* — the value simply never arrived.

\- \*\*Fix\*\*: \`url\` carries a plain string value and is now handled exactly like

  \`string\`. Both "Create a new alert" and "Create a new case" are affected, as

  they share the same parsing routine.

\- \*\*No more silence\*\*: a custom field dropped because its type is unmapped, or

  because its value does not match its declared type, is now logged as a

  warning (\`THC-117\`) naming both the field and the type. A future unknown type

  will be visible in the logs instead of costing a day of troubleshooting.

\- \*\*Regression tests\*\*: the parsing routine gains its first unit tests. Every

  TheHive custom field type is now asserted to survive, and the "dropped but

  logged" behaviour is asserted too.



\### 🖥️ Dashboards: the Job SID is now required (\[#132]\(https://github.com/LetMeR00t/TA-thehive-cortex/issues/132))

\- \*\*Root cause\*\*: "Job SID (input data)" was optional in the \*Create a new

  case\* and \*Create a new alert\* panels. Leaving it empty produced an empty

  \`| loadjob\`, and the failure surfaced far from its cause — a

  \`FileNotFoundError\` followed by \`UnboundLocalError: local variable 'rf'

  referenced before assignment\`, deep inside the alert action base.

\- \*\*Fix\*\*: Splunk Simple XML has no \`required\` attribute, so the field now

  drives a token and the action panel depends on it. The action cannot run

  until a SID is entered, and the label carries a \`\*\` like the other mandatory

  fields.



\### ☁️ Splunk Cloud: \`sc\_admin\` can write views and navigation

\- \`metadata/default.meta\` granted write access on \`\[views]\` and \`\[nav]\` to the

  \`admin\` role only. Splunk Cloud customers hold \*\*\`sc\_admin\`\*\*, not \`admin\`,

  so those knowledge objects were unreachable for them. Both roles are now

  granted, matching what the app-level stanza already did.



\### 📚 Documentation (\[#128]\(https://github.com/LetMeR00t/TA-thehive-cortex/issues/128))

\- The UC2 walkthrough screenshots predate the v4.0.0 UCC rework: they still

  show \*TheHive instance ID\* as free text and \*Alert mode\* as radio buttons,

  where both are now dropdowns named \*\*Instance\*\* and \*\*Alert mode\*\*.

\- The screenshots could not be regenerated for this release, so the section now

  carries the \*\*field values in writing\*\*, read off the images themselves,

  including the fact that \`Severity\`, \`TLP\`, \`PAP\` and \`Scope\` are dropdowns

  rather than field names, and that \`Description\` expects the \*\*name of the

  field\*\* holding the text (\`info\` in the UC2 search).



\## Under the hood



These change nothing for users, but matter to anyone building the add-on:



\- \*\*\`splunktaucclib\` 8.1.0 → 8.2.0\*\*, the minimum accepted by \`ucc-gen\` 6.5.3.

  Building with an older pin fails before any code is compiled.

\- \*\*\`package/lib/requirements.txt\` is now versioned.\*\* It was silently excluded

  by the generic \`lib/\` rule of the Python \`.gitignore\`, which meant a fresh

  clone could not rebuild the same add-on.

\- \*\*The test suite is now part of the repository.\*\* The unit tests mock every

  Splunk and network module and run anywhere; the integration tests read their

  endpoints and credentials from a local \`.env\`, which stays out of the

  repository.

\- \`CONTRIBUTE.md\` gains the \*\*AppInspect step\*\*, which the build/package/deploy

  lifecycle did not describe.



\## Splunk Cloud vetting



Measured with AppInspect \*\*4.3.0\*\* (\`--mode precert --included-tags cloud\`) on

the packaged \`.spl\`:



\| | |

\| :--- | :--- |

\| \`error\` / \`failure\` | \*\*0 / 0\*\* |

\| \`future\_failure\` | 1 |

\| \`warning\` | 15 (all informational) |

\| \`success\` | 136 |



The remaining \`future\_failure\` is \`check\_for\_custom\_mako\_templates\`, on

\`appserver/templates/base.html\`. \*\*It cannot be fixed from this repository\*\*:

the file does not exist in the sources — \`ucc-gen\` generates it, the latest

release (6.5.3) still does, and three generated views reference it

(\`configuration.xml\`, \`dashboard.xml\`, \`inputs.xml\`). AppInspect advises

regenerating with UCC ≥ 6.3.0, which does not remove it. It becomes blocking

with Splunk Enterprise 10.4; the fix has to come from a future UCC release.



\## Deployment Notes

\- \*\*Prerequisite\*\*: Python 3.9 (matches Splunk's bundled interpreter).

\- \*\*Migration Path\*\*:

    \- \*\*From v4.2.1 / v4.2.0 / v4.1.0 / v4.0.0\*\*: non-breaking update. Existing

      configuration, accounts, instances and certificates are preserved.

    \- \*\*From v3.9.0 (Direct Upgrade)\*\*: you can upgrade directly to v4.2.2.

    \- \*\*⚠️ CRITICAL\*\*: if upgrading from v3.x, the

      \*\*\[v4.0.0 migration instructions]\(./v4.0.0.md) are mandatory\*\* and remain

      valid for this version (UCC architecture migration, breaking configuration

      changes, and new credential storage). Please read them carefully before

      proceeding.

\- \*\*After upgrading\*\*: if you use a custom field of type \`url\` in an alert

  action, it will start arriving in TheHive — check that the receiving custom

  field is the one you expect.

\- \*\*Upgrade tip (Windows / on-prem)\*\*: never delete the app's \`local/\` folder.

  Stop Splunk, back up \`local/\`, deploy the new build, restore \`local/\`, then

  start Splunk.

**# Release Notes - v4.2.1: "The Honey Keeper" 🍯**




**## Summary**

Version 4.2.1 is a **\*\*hotfix release\*\*** addressing a data-loss regression

introduced in v4.1.0: the \`thehive\_datatypes.csv\` lookup could be periodically

**\*\*overwritten with default values\*\***, wiping out user-defined custom field

mappings and causing observables to go missing from TheHive alerts and cases.

No new feature is introduced and no configuration change is required — this is

a safe, drop-in update from v4.2.0.




**## Improvements & Bug Fixes**




**### 🗂️ Alert Actions: custom datatype mappings are no longer lost**

\- **\*\*Root cause\*\***: since v4.1.0, alert actions refresh the

  \`thehive\_datatypes.csv\` lookup from the TheHive API whenever the file is

  older than 24 hours. The refresh rebuilt the file **\*\*from scratch\*\*** with only

  the native observable types returned by TheHive, silently destroying every

  custom row (e.g. \`src\_ip → ip\`, \`dest\_domain → domain\`) that detections rely

  on to map Splunk fields to observables. In practice the lookup was reset

  every 24-72 hours, depending on when the next alert action fired.

\- **\*\*Fix — non-destructive merge\*\***: the periodic refresh is kept (it still

  picks up new observable types created in TheHive), but it now \*\*preserves

  every existing row\*\* of the lookup, custom mappings included. Only datatypes

  not already listed are appended. A full regeneration never happens once the

  file exists.

\- **\*\*Atomic writes\*\***: the lookup is now written to a uniquely-named temporary

  file and moved into place atomically, so a crash or two concurrent alert

  actions can no longer leave a truncated or half-written lookup behind.

\- **\*\*Safety guard\*\***: if the existing lookup cannot be read (locked, malformed

  encoding, permissions), the refresh is **\*\*aborted\*\*** instead of overwriting

  content that could not be preserved (logged as \`THC-4\`).




**### 🧹 Minor**

\- Fixed a file-handle leak in the datatype lookup reader (the file was opened

  on every alert action run but never closed).




**## Deployment Notes**

\- **\*\*Prerequisite\*\***: Python 3.9 (matches Splunk's bundled interpreter).

\- **\*\*After upgrading\*\***: if your custom \`thehive\_datatypes.csv\` was recently

  reset, restore it once from your backup — it will no longer be overwritten.

\- **\*\*Migration Path\*\***:

    - **\*\*From v4.2.0 / v4.1.0 / v4.0.0\*\***: non-breaking update. Existing

      configuration, accounts, instances and certificates are preserved.

    - **\*\*From v3.9.0 (Direct Upgrade)\*\***: you can upgrade directly to v4.2.1.

    - **\*\*⚠️ CRITICAL\*\***: if upgrading from v3.x, the

      **\*\*\[v4.0.0 migration instructions]\(**<u>./v4.0.0.md</u>**) are mandatory\*\*** and remain

      valid for this version (UCC architecture migration, breaking configuration

      changes, and new credential storage). Please read them carefully before

      proceeding.

\- **\*\*Upgrade tip (Windows / on-prem)\*\***: never delete the app's \`local/\` folder.

  Stop Splunk, back up \`local/\`, deploy the new build, restore \`local/\`, then

  start Splunk.

\# Release Notes



\## Summary

Version 4.2.0 is a \*\*stability and reliability release\*\*. It hardens the alert actions and adaptive responses (alert/case creation), fixes several observable parsing edge cases that could silently drop data or get the whole payload rejected by TheHive, and corrects date/timestamp handling in TTP processing and the Cases LIST search command. No new feature is introduced and no configuration change is required — this is a safe, drop-in update from v4.1.0.



\## Improvements & Bug Fixes



\### 🧩 Alert Actions: robust observable parsing

\- \*\*Valid observable sub-field types\*\*: observable sub-fields are now read with

  their documented \`snake\_case\` names (\`\<field>:is\_ioc\`, \`\<field>:sighted\`,

  \`\<field>:sighted\_at\`, \`\<field>:ignore\_similarity\`) and coerced to the native

  types TheHive expects. Previously the boolean \`sighted\` value was forwarded as

  the raw string \`"1"\`, causing TheHive to reject the request with

  \`BadRequest - Invalid json\` and silently dropping \`is\_ioc\`, \`sighted\_at\` and

  \`ignore\_similarity\`. The sighting timestamp now also accepts float epoch

  values and is normalized to milliseconds.

\- \*\*Multi-value observable splitting\*\*: fixed a regex that split observable

  values on the literal letter \`n\` instead of a newline, which mangled

  multi-value observables.

\- \*\*Resilient row handling\*\*: improved handling of sanitized rows to avoid

  \`KeyError\` exceptions on incomplete events, and corrected the \`sourceRef\`

  variable used in debug logging.



\### 📎 Alert Actions: reliable result attachments

\- Result attachments (\`attach\_results\`) now use a \*\*uniquely-named temporary

  directory per invocation\*\* instead of a fixed file name in the shared system

  temp directory. On Windows (where \`splunkd\` runs as the SYSTEM service and the

  temp directory is \`C:\WINDOWS\TEMP\`), the previous behavior caused concurrent

  or overlapping runs to collide on the same path, raising

  \`Permission denied\` / \`No such file or directory\` and \*\*preventing the second

  alert/case of a multi-result search from being created\*\* (e.g. UC2 — "Saved

  search, several alerts"). Temp files are now always cleaned up, and the

  attachment result is guarded against \`None\`.



\### ⏱️ TTP & timestamp handling

\- \`\_time\` is now parsed as a \*\*float\*\* when processing TTPs, preventing failures

  on sub-second timestamps.

\- When the configured \`timestamp\_field\` is missing from an event, processing now

  \*\*falls back to the current time\*\* instead of failing.



\### 🔎 Search commands

\- \*\*Cases LIST respects Date settings (#126)\*\*: the Cases LIST action now

  correctly applies the configured date range instead of ignoring it.



\## Deployment Notes

\- \*\*Prerequisite\*\*: Python 3.9 (matches Splunk's bundled interpreter).

\- \*\*Migration Path\*\*:

    \- \*\*From v4.1.0 / v4.0.0\*\*: non-breaking update. Existing configuration,

      accounts, instances and certificates are preserved.

    \- \*\*From v3.9.0 (Direct Upgrade)\*\*: you can upgrade directly to v4.2.0.

    \- \*\*⚠️ CRITICAL\*\*: if upgrading from v3.x, the

      \*\*\[v4.0.0 migration instructions]\(./v4.0.0.md) are mandatory\*\* and remain

      valid for this version (UCC architecture migration, breaking configuration

      changes, and new credential storage). Please read them carefully before

      proceeding.

\- \*\*Upgrade tip (Windows / on-prem)\*\*: never delete the app's \`local/\` folder.

  Stop Splunk, back up \`local/\`, deploy the new build, restore \`local/\`, then

  start Splunk.

# Release Notes

## Summary

Version 4.1.0 introduces significant enhancements to user interaction and data enrichment capabilities between Splunk and TheHive/Cortex. This release focuses on investigation workflows, periodic data collection, visual identity, and operational robustness.

## Deployment Notes

- **Prerequisite**: Python 3.9+ (as per UCC standard).
- **Migration Path**:
    - **From v4.0.0**: This is a non-breaking update. Existing configuration is preserved.
    - **From v3.9.0 (Direct Upgrade)**: You can upgrade directly from v3.9.0 to v4.1.0 without installing v4.0.0 first.
      - **⚠️ CRITICAL**: If upgrading from v3.x, the **[v4.0.0 migration instructions](https://github.com/LetMeR00t/TA-thehive-cortex/releases/tag/v4.0.0) are mandatory** and remain valid for this version (UCC architecture migration, breaking configuration changes, and new credential storage). Please read them carefully before proceeding.

## New Features

### 📅 New Modular Inputs: Tasks, Timeline & Status
Three new data collection mechanisms have been added to track your cases and platform health:

- **TheHive Tasks Collection**: Periodically retrieve all tasks associated with cases for better operational monitoring.
- **TheHive Timeline Collection**: Automatically fetch case timeline events to build a complete history of investigations in Splunk.
- **TheHive Instance Status**: Monitor your TheHive instances' health, version, and license status directly from Splunk.
- **Backfill Support**: Dedicated backfill scripts are available for Tasks and Timeline to recover historical data.

### 🛡️ Add Timeline Event Alert Action
A new Custom Alert Action (and Adaptive Response) **"TheHive - Add timeline event"** is now available.

- Analysts can now automatically or manually push findings directly to a case's timeline.
- Supports custom titles (with `<inheritance>` from search name), descriptions, and specific start/end dates.
- Fully integrated into the **Audit Logs** dashboard for tracking.

### 🔢 Automatic Case Number Resolution
The Add-on now handles both internal IDs (`~12345`) and human-readable case numbers (`2392`).

- If a case number is provided in any alert action (Add Observables, Add Timeline Event), the app automatically resolves it to the correct internal ID via the API.
- This simplifies workflows for analysts who primarily work with case numbers in the UI.

### 🎨 High-Quality Visual Identity
All Custom Alert Actions have been updated with **unique, high-resolution hexagonal icons**.

- **TheHive Actions**: Official Yellow (`#FFC107`) branding.
- **Cortex Actions**: Official Light Blue (`#87CEFA`) branding.
- Optimized with transparent backgrounds for seamless integration into Splunk's Dark and Light themes.

## Improvements & Bug Fixes

### ⏱️ Standardized Polling Intervals

- Implemented **dynamic interval flooring** across all modular inputs (`thehive_tasks`, `thehive_timeline`, `thehive_alerts_cases`, etc.).
- All collection time ranges are now aligned to clean boundaries (e.g., `12:51:00` to `12:52:00`), eliminating "seconds drift" in logs and search results.

### 📊 Enhanced Audit Logs Dashboard
The **Audit Logs** dashboard has been significantly updated to provide better operational visibility:

- Comprehensive Action Tracking: Now includes dedicated filters and metrics for all Custom Alert Actions, including the new Timeline Event action.
- Data Collection Monitoring: The dashboard now tracks the execution and results of the new modular inputs (Tasks, Timeline, and Status), ensuring full traceability of your data ingestion.
- Improved Success Monitoring: Logic updated to track specific event codes (e.g., `TH201` for successful timeline events, `CAA-THCA-125` for cases), allowing for clear distinction between successful creations and operational issues.

### 🔧 Indexing & Props

- Fixed `thehive:timeline` sourcetype to ensure Splunk prioritizes normalized `_time` from JSON payloads.
- Cleaned up build process to automatically remove Windows binaries (`.exe`, `.pyd`), Python compiled files (`.pyc`), and caches for Splunk Cloud compatibility.

# Release Notes: TA-thehive-cortex v4.0.0 ## ⚠️ CRITICAL: Breaking Changes Version 4.0.0 introduces a **complete architectural migration to the Splunk UCC Framework**. This is a major breaking change that requires manual intervention for existing users: 1. **Configuration Incompatibility:** Configuration files (`.conf`) from version 3.9.x and earlier are **not compatible** as instance management has moved from a manually managed CSV lookup (`thehive_datatypes.csv`) to a dedicated **UCC REST API** endpoint and configuration file (`thehive_cortex_instances.conf`). 2. **Credential Migration:** Credentials are now stored securely using Splunk's standard **Storage Passwords** through the UCC interface. Previous API keys and passwords might not be working and should be set up from scratch. 3. **Modular Input Normalization:** Input stanzas and sourcetypes have been normalized for better consistency. Existing inputs will not be recognized and **must be re-created** via the new "Inputs" page. | Entity | Legacy Sourcetype (v3.9.0) | New Sourcetype (v4.0.0) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Cases** | `thehive:last_created:cases`
`thehive:last_updated:cases` | `thehive:cases:createdAt`
`thehive:cases:updatedAt`
`thehive:cases:startDate` | | **Alerts** | `thehive:last_created:alerts`
`thehive:last_updated:alerts` | `thehive:alerts:createdAt`
`thehive:alerts:updatedAt`

To simplify the transition, dedicated **macros** have been included to search across both legacy and new sourcetypes: | Entity | Migration Macro | Included Sourcetypes (Legacy & New) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Cases** | `` `thehive_cases` `` | `thehive:last_created:cases`, `thehive:last_updated:cases`, `thehive:cases:*` | | **Alerts** | `` `thehive_alerts` `` | `thehive:last_created:alerts`, `thehive:last_updated:alerts`, `thehive:alerts:*` | | **Observables**| `` `thehive_observables` `` | `thehive:last_created:observables`, `thehive:last_updated:observables`, `thehive:observables:*` | | **Audit Logs** | `` `thehive_audit` `` | `thehive:last_created:audit`, `thehive:audit` | | **Tasks** | `` `thehive_tasks` `` | `thehive:last_created:case_tasks`, `thehive:last_updated:case_tasks`, `thehive:tasks:*` | 5. **Python 3.x Requirement:** This version is optimized for the latest Python 3 versions supported by Splunk (Python 3.9+). It follows modern Splunk development standards, ensuring better performance and security compliance across Splunk 9.x environments. 6. **Simplified Custom CA Management:** While SSL verification remains mandatory for HTTPS connections, the process for using self-signed certificates has been simplified. You can now place your custom CA certificate bundle (PEM format) directly in the app's `local/` folder and reference its filename in the **Instance** configuration. --- ## 🔄 User Experience: What's different? (v3.9.0 vs v4.0.0) | Feature | Legacy (v3.9.0) | UCC Framework (v4.0.0) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Configuration UI** | Single, legacy Splunk setup page with manual instance management (lookups) and lack of automated information loading. | Modern, tabbed interface (**Accounts**, **Instances**, **Settings**) with improved field rendering. Instances are now centralized, linked to Accounts, and easily selectable via dropdowns across the app. | | **Credential Storage** | Custom `.conf` file (often plain text or legacy encryption). | **Reinforced security and efficiency** for accessing Splunk standard Storage Passwords. | | **Input Management** | Managed via standard Splunk Inputs menu with fragmented manual configurations for regular and backfill inputs. | Dedicated **Inputs** page with **harmonized groups** merging regular collection and one-shot (backfill) services on the same page. | | **Dashboards** | Legacy search logic. | **Improved efficiency and readiness** with optimized field coloring and better error handling. | --- ## 🛠 Upgrade Procedure (Migration from v3.9.x) To successfully migrate from a previous version to v4.0.0, you **MUST** follow one of the cleanup methods below: ### 1. Pre-Migration Audit * Record your current TheHive/Cortex URLs, Port, and API Keys/Credentials. * Note down your active Modular Inputs (Index, Interval, and specific filters). ### 2. Migration Options (Cleanup) Choose the method that fits your environment to avoid configuration conflicts: * **Option A: Clean Installation (Recommended for Single Servers)** * **Stop Splunk.** * **Backup and Remove:** Backup your old app folder, then **delete** the `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/TA-thehive-cortex` directory entirely. This ensures no legacy scripts or incompatible XML views remain. * **Option B: Manual In-Place Preparation (No restart required)** * **Empty Legacy Configs:** In your current version, remove all manual configurations from the `local/` folder (specifically `inputs.conf` and `thehive_cortex.conf`). This "cleans" the environment before proceeding with the standard app upgrade. * **Option C: Deployment Server (Distributed Environments)** * **De-assign:** Remove the legacy app from its Server Class. * **Purge & Replace:** Delete the app from `deployment-apps`, replace it with the v4.0.0 package, and re-assign. Ensure **Forwarders and Search Heads** have their `local/` configurations cleaned as per Option B if necessary. *Note: If you want to keep your historical data indexed in Splunk, do not delete the indexes themselves. Historical raw data remains identical and searchable despite the new sourcetype naming convention.* ### 3. Installation & Re-configuration * **Install v4.0.0:** Deploy the new package and **Start Splunk** (if stopped). * *Note for developers: If you are building the app yourself, you MUST use Python 3.9 with the UCC generator to ensure the final package is compatible.* * **Configure Accounts:** Navigate to *Configuration > Accounts* and add your TheHive and Cortex credentials. * **Configure Instances:** Navigate to *Configuration > Instances*. Define your server details and link them to the appropriate Account. * *Note: If you have just created a new Account, you must refresh the page to ensure it appears in the Account selection dropdown when creating an Instance.* * **Review Settings:** Check the *Settings* tab for global parameters (Max Jobs, Sort orders, etc.). ### 4. Input Restoration * Navigate to the **Inputs** page. * Re-create your collection tasks (e.g., Alerts & Cases) using the new service groups. * *Tip: Use the new **Backfill (One-shot)** inputs if you need to recover data from the period during which the app was being upgraded.* --- ## 📝 Detailed Change Log ### ✨ Features * **Compatibility Matrix:** * **Splunk Enterprise:** 9.2 and above (minimum) * **Splunk Enterprise Security:** 7.x and above (minimum) * **Common Information Model (CIM):** 4.x and above (minimum) * **Autonomous Modular Inputs Architecture:** Complete rewrite of the collection engine for increased stability and independent processing of Alerts and Cases. * **Historical Backfill Support:** Introduction of "One-shot" inputs for historical data recovery with the capability to specify a starting and ending date or datetime. * **"Occurred Time" Support:** Alerts can now be collected based on their actual occurrence date in TheHive 5 (#121). * **Advanced Input Selection:** Implementation of a `checkboxTree` UI for precise selection of metadata (Observables, TTPs, Tasks, Pages). * **Multi-Tenancy & Organizations:** Added "Organisation" support for TheHive 5 instances, visible directly in the configuration table and accessible through REST API. ### 🐞 Bug Fixes * **MITRE ATT&CK Parsing:** Fixed critical `IndexError` and improved alignment for multi-value TTPs from Splunk ES (#110). * **Alert Creation Robustness:** Fixed failure when `th_severity` is missing for certain alerts (#115). * **Multi-value Field Normalization:** Robust parsing of Splunk multi-value fields and tags to prevent batch failures during export (#112). * **Dashboard Reliability:** Resolved search blocking issues in `cases.xml` and restored field coloring in Audit logs. * **Backslash Handling:** Improved sanitization of backslashes in instance hostnames and dropdowns. ### 🔧 Other Changes * **UCC 6.x Migration:** Full compliance with the latest Splunk UCC standards and `globalConfig.json` schema. * **Standardized Library Management:** Replaced legacy `aob_py3` remnants with a clean `libs/` folder containing updated and versioned `thehive4py` and `cortex4py`. Libraries are now managed via UCC, making upgrades easier to maintain and ensuring better compatibility. * **AppInspect Validation:** Removed redundant Windows binaries (.exe, .pyd) and optimized metadata for Cloud/AppInspect compliance. * **Refined Logging:** Enhanced logging system with `exec_id` propagation across all Modular Inputs and Alert Actions for easier troubleshooting.
